en: Thus far in this section, you saw examples
for task-specific agents. And indeed, it is
quite likely that if you're going to build
agents manually,
they will be task-specific, purpose-built
for the requirements of your business or in
your day-to-day work. But of course, you
could also be building general, more generic
agents. And if we take another look at the
core building blocks you should consider
when both building or using an AI agent. Of
course, we saw that for the task-specific
agents, we covered these blocks here. We
obviously needed a model. We obviously
needed tools, task-specific tools. And we
also had instructions, albeit rather short
instructions, but nonetheless instructions.
Now, for a generic or more general agent,
you also may wanna support agent skills. As
you learned, that is a standard, but of
course, if your agent doesn't support it, if
you didn't add the logic to look for and
load skills,
it's not worth anything. And the same is
true for memory. And regarding instructions,
you also may want to load agents'MD files
and consider those as well. So
you may want to add more things to your
agent that allow it, and therefore the user
using it, to provide more useful context to
the agent. And obviously another important
part will be that you want more generic
tools so that your agent is not
purpose-built for one specific task, but
instead can tackle a versatile range of
tasks. And that's what we'll explore in the
next example.
